subject: On-prem gateway: off-ramp connector recommendation and next steps
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme-health.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: netops@acme-health.com
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment connectivity — Acme ask and constraints

Hi Jordan / Kim,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Acme Health is moving forward with a pilot of Redwood Private in our primary datacenter (on‑prem colocation) and NetOps asked me to get a recommended connectivity pattern so we can scope firewall changes and procurement. High level constraints: 

- Data residency + strict ingress filtering (no public internet egress from our infra to hosted endpoints)
- Low single‑digit ms latency requirement for inference traffic to keep sync features performant
- Auditability: we need connection audit logs and proof of key custody for compliance
- Network team wants a solution that minimizes long‑term VPN appliance maintenance

Can you provide: a short recommendation (VPC Peering vs PrivateLink vs site‑to‑site VPN), a list of required network artifacts (CIDR ranges, ports, certs), and whether we should do a canary (yes/no)? I attached our network requirements spreadsheet and the internal NetOps notes.

Ideal delivery: a one‑page recommendation + connector diagram and a small runbook for the pilot.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Chen
Director, Cloud Integrations — Acme Health

Attachments: acme-network-reqs.xlsx

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme-health.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — Acme ask and constraints

Alice — thanks for the clear summary and the sheet; good context. Quick take up front so you can share with NetOps:

- Short recommendation: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) as the primary pattern, with a lightweight site‑to‑site VPN as a failover for maintenance windows or when cross‑VPC features are needed.
- Why: PrivateLink minimizes attack surface (no public NAT), provides per‑customer endpoints we can instrument for audit logs, and fits your desire to avoid broad peering across accounts.
- Tradeoffs: PrivateLink has higher per‑GB egress costs and requires endpoint ENIs in your VPC/subnet model. Peering would be cheaper and lower latency but exposes your VPC ranges to Redwood and complicates cross‑tenant isolation and routing policies. A pure S2S VPN is simplest to implement quickly but increases operational burden on VPN appliances and has less granular observability.

Questions to finalize the recommendation:
1) Can you confirm whether Acme wants a dedicated VPC for Redwood only, or to host the interface endpoints in a shared services VPC?
2) Do you have any maximum sustained throughput targets (Gbps) per‑site we should budget for?
3) Are there restrictions on creating ENIs in the subnets you’d use for endpoints?

I’ve looped in Kim (networking) to validate the ENI/runbook bits. If that looks OK I’ll send a 1‑page with diagram and a pilot runbook (canary plan + test vectors) by Monday.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: offramp-checklist-v1.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 08:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment connectivity — tech tradeoffs / latency numbers

Forwarding my notes on latency/cost/ops tradeoffs so we have concrete bullets for Acme. Summary below — feel free to paste into the one‑pager.

--- my notes ---
Pattern: PrivateLink (interface endpoint)
Pros:
- Strong tenant isolation (no route table exchanges)
- Endpoint level metrics (we can attach flow logs + per‑ENI counters)
- Compatible with our Dedicated control plane model and per‑customer key management
Cons:
- ENI IP exhaustion risk in dense subnet setups — need guidance on subnet sizing
- Slightly higher per‑token cost projection due to egress billing (estimate +8–15%)

Pattern: VPC Peering
Pros:
- Lowest latency (no proxying), minimal per‑GB cost
- Simpler for bi‑directional low‑latency traffic (if you need callbacks)
Cons:
- Requires route propagation and peering acceptance, increases blast radius
- Not compatible with multi‑tenant Hosted model; still OK for Private if both sides agree

Pattern: Site‑to‑Site VPN
Pros:
- Fast to provision in many shops, works across provider boundaries
- No need to manage ENIs; keeps Redwood traffic over an encrypted tunnel
Cons:
- Appliances require maintenance, MTU/path MTU issues cause splits and fragmentation
- Less visibility into per‑connection token metrics; harder to attribute traffic for billing

Latency table (ballpark, us‑west region):
- VPC Peering: 1–4 ms RTT
- PrivateLink: 3–8 ms RTT (additional proxy hop)
- S2S VPN: 8–30 ms RTT (appliance dependent)

Operational recommendation:
- Pilot: PrivateLink in a dedicated Acme VPC + S2S VPN as failover. Run a 2‑week canary (10–20% traffic) with detailed latency and error monitoring. If peering is requested later for low‑latency callbacks, scope a controlled peering engagement.

Attachments I recommend including in the customer packet: redwood‑privatedeploy‑cnx‑diagram.pdf (high level), subnet ENI sizing worksheet, and a test plan.

Ben
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment connectivity — tech tradeoffs / latency numbers

Quoting Ben — adding operational checklist and test plan items we should require from Acme before pilot: 

Requirements checklist (Network artifacts we need):
- CIDR ranges for the endpoint subnets (3 AZs preferred) and confirmation ENI quotas allow 50+ endpoints per AZ
- Explicit egress firewall rules: ports 443 outbound to Redwood interface endpoint ENIs + management ports (TCP 22/3389) if remote troubleshooting is required (we prefer SSH jump hosts rather than open management ports)
- Service account + static IPs for monitoring probes (to create allowlist entries)
- Shared TLS cert provisioning plan: who manages cert rotation (we support both customer‑managed and Redwood KMS certs)
- NetOps contact and maintenance windows for routing changes

Test plan (canary):
- Canary window: 2 weeks, 15% production traffic routed to PrivateLink connector
- Success criteria: median tokenizer latency within 120% of baseline, P95 below 2x baseline, error rate <0.1%
- Observability: per‑endpoint flow logs enabled, token accounting tags included in request headers for attribution
- Rollback: automatic traffic shift to S2S VPN if P95 latency exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive 10‑minute windows

Runbook snippets:
- If endpoint ENI flaps: collect flow logs, check subnet IP utilization, resend provisioning request for replacement ENI
- If P95 spikes: shift 50% traffic to VPN path and open ops channel; if persistent, pause pilot and escalate to infra on call

I can draft the runbook templates and the small playbook for NetOps (detailed firewall rules + CIDR examples) once we get the UID ranges from Acme.

Connor O'Brien
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme-health.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — Acme ask and constraints

Alice — thanks for the original note and for looping NetOps. Attached is a short packet that contains: 1) one‑page recommendation (we propose PrivateLink primary + S2S VPN failover), 2) connector diagram, 3) pilot runbook and test vectors, and 4) a checklist of the network artifacts we need from Acme.

Next steps (proposed):
- Can you confirm whether Acme will host endpoints in a dedicated Acme VPC or a shared services VPC? (If dedicated, we will provide exact ENI sizing guidance).
- Please share the CIDR ranges you plan to use for the endpoint subnets (ideally three AZs).
- Suggested pilot window: May 17–31 (2 weeks). Can you confirm availability for a short kickoff on May 12?

If that all sounds good I’ll send the packet over your procurement contact and open a HubSpot ticket (linked). We’ll also include a DocuSign change order for the pilot increment under ACME‑2027‑EXP‑47 if you want to proceed.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
